clue.text: To be a visitor, put down your name and ID

parts.note: to call on someone is to pay them a visit
to sign is to write your name on something

explanation.surface: Instructions at a reception desk: sign in and show identification.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a visitors' book instruction, but 'ID' is the definition: a radio operator's identifying code.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio station's or operator's identifying code is its broadcast identity, a kind of identification.

clue.text: Pillar in paper

definitions.meaning: a regular feature or vertical block of print in a newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names an architectural support and a newspaper feature or block of text.

clue.text: A revolutionary force for students

definitions.note: by the setter's special rule, an 'A' opening a clue always means astronomer

parts.note: love is the force said to make the world go round
L is a learner, so LL is learners or students

explanation.surface: Someone is described as a radical power on behalf of the student body.
explanation.walkthrough: By the setter's rule a leading 'A' means astronomer. 'Revolutionary force' plays on the saying that love makes the world go round. Sir Bernard Lovell founded the Jodrell Bank radio telescope.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Bernard Lovell was a British radio astronomer, founder of the Jodrell Bank observatory.

clue.text: Leap year's beginning?

definitions.meaning: the season that comes at the start of the natural year

explanation.surface: A question about the leap year and how it begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leap year' looks like one phrase, but it splits into two definitions: a jump, and the season that opens the year.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump is to bound; the first season of the growing year shares the same word.

clue.text: Verbal opposition to succeed with detective story writer

parts.note: to gain is to succeed in getting something
Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels

explanation.surface: Someone wins out with the help of a crime novelist, against spoken objections.
explanation.definitionFit: People who contradict or deny something are its spoken opponents, those voicing objection.

clue.text: Change second of three in Macbeth?

parts.note: the three witches of Shakespeare's Macbeth; one of them is a witch

explanation.surface: A theatre note about altering the second of the weird sisters in Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap one thing for another is to change it.

clue.text: Military doctor gets medal for clothing

parts.note: war is the business of the military
OBE, Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: An army doctor is decorated for supplying uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's whole stock of clothes is their wardrobe, by extension from the cupboard.

clue.text: Slider puts old coat round standard on pole

indicators.note: in a down clue the pole sits below, placed on the end
the coat goes around the standard, enclosing it

parts.note: a toga was the ancient Roman garment
bog standard means ordinary, so bog stands in for standard
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A sledger wears an old coat wrapped around a flagpole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is BOG from the British phrase 'bog standard' (ordinary).
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge for coasting down snowy slopes is something that slides.

clue.text: A lady's at sea in London

definitions.note: by the setter's special rule, an 'A' opening a clue always means astronomer

parts.note: something belonging to a lady is hers

indicators.note: the letters before sea in the London district are what is wanted, so sea is taken off

parts.note: Chelsea is a district of London
the word as written, removed from the district's name

explanation.surface: A woman is out at sea somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: CHELSEA is a London district; 'at sea' says CHEL plus SEA make it, so CHEL is what remains once SEA is taken away. 'A' means astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: William Herschel discovered Uranus; his sister Caroline and son John were also noted astronomers.

clue.text: Danger here — of hepatitis suggested?

parts.note: an electrified railway track is dangerous, and the phrase sounds like a disease of the organ hepatitis affects

explanation.definitionFit: An electrified rail carrying current is dangerous to touch, a hazard on electric railways.

clue.text: Name of Welshman detailed by investigator

indicators.note: de-tailed: the last letter is cut off the name

parts.note: Probert is a Welsh surname, as in Rosie Probert of Under Milk Wood

explanation.surface: A Welsh name is spelt out in detail by a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'set out in detail', but it means de-tailed: lose the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who probes, digging into a matter, is an investigator.

clue.text: Motorway part, southeast Italian

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI
a lane is one part of a motorway carriageway
SE is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A road description: a section of the motorway heading southeast.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway from London to Leeds, crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Milan is an Italian person.

clue.text: Very sad time with trashy paper in charge

parts.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A gloomy moment when a tabloid is running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragic is deeply sorrowful, like a calamity.

clue.text: Revolutionary oriental Jew that eats dairy produce

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
E for east, oriental meaning eastern
a Semite, loosely a Jewish person

explanation.surface: A Marxist from the East who is Jewish and eats milk products.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny arachnid that infests and feeds on stored cheese is a creature feeding on dairy food.

clue.text: A in theory Bach composed

definitions.note: by the setter's special rule, an 'A' opening a clue always means astronomer

indicators.note: the letters are put together in a new order, as a piece is composed

explanation.surface: A music theory exercise written in the style of Bach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' fits Bach but is the anagram signal for THEORY BACH. 'A' means astronomer: Tycho Brahe, the Danish observer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tycho Brahe was the Danish nobleman whose precise naked-eye observations of planets underpinned later work.

clue.text: Effect of fire largely over glass in Russian city

indicators.note: in a down clue the smoke piece sits around and above the glass
most of the word, so its final letter is cut

parts.note: smoke is what a fire produces
a lens is a piece of shaped glass

explanation.surface: Smoke from a fire hangs above glass in a Russian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' means all but the last letter, and 'over' places the fire's product around and above the glass in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Smolensk is a historic city in western Russia on the Dnieper.

clue.text: Drug chic up here to catch car

indicators.note: in a down clue the run is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
smart means stylish

explanation.surface: A trendy drug spot where people catch a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' in a down clue turns POTSMART around. 'Car' here is a tramcar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopping place for trams is where passengers board a streetcar.

clue.text: Top 50 in boat

parts.note: a pinnace is a ship's small boat
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people on a boat at the peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or peak of something is its summit.

clue.text: A with money about to invest in the horses?

definitions.note: by the setter's special rule, an 'A' opening a clue always means astronomer

indicators.note: to invest is to place inside, so these go within the horses

parts.note: mares are female horses
tin is old slang for money
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: Someone with cash is about to put money on the racehorses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest in the horses' suggests betting; it means put inside MARES. Lord Martin Rees is the Astronomer Royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Martin Rees is Britain's Astronomer Royal, a cosmologist at Cambridge.

clue.text: A year's opening under orchestra

definitions.note: by the setter's special rule, an 'A' opening a clue always means astronomer

indicators.note: in a down clue this letter comes below the orchestra

parts.note: the Hallé is a Manchester orchestra

indicators.note: the opening of the year is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone opens the year playing beneath an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hallé is a famous orchestra based in Manchester. 'A' means astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmond Halley predicted the return of the comet now named after him.

clue.text: A centre of revolution with some bleeding

definitions.note: by the setter's special rule, an 'A' opening a clue always means astronomer

parts.note: a hub is the centre a wheel revolves around

indicators.note: only some of the word is used: its first three letters, with the ending dropped

explanation.surface: Someone at the heart of an uprising is bleeding a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests uprising; it is a wheel turning around its HUB. 'A' means astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin Hubble showed that galaxies lie beyond the Milky Way and that the universe expands.

clue.text: Edict of French and native American

parts.note: de is French for of
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: An order issued by the French and a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: An official order issued by an authority is an edict.

clue.text: Breakfast time to break fast with sad song

indicators.note: the morning breaks into the fast, sitting inside it

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
AM, the morning, when breakfast is eaten

explanation.surface: Breakfast ends a fast, accompanied by a mournful tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue puns on 'breakfast' as 'break fast': the morning hours are set inside the season of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful song or poem is an elegy or dirge.

clue.text: Spoil one in the set

indicators.note: the one goes inside the set

parts.note: a denture is a set of false teeth
A means one, a single

explanation.surface: Ruining one item in a matching collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The set' is a set of false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To change something's essential nature, especially making it unfit, is to spoil it.

clue.text: Books in pleasant spot

indicators.note: the books go inside the pleasant word

parts.note: nice means pleasant
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Reading books in a lovely place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a noun (place) but is the verb: to observe.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or observe it.

clue.text: Political economist first with lawyers to create some pressure

parts.note: John Stuart Mill wrote on political economy
I is one, first
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: An economist and lawyers lobby to apply pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of atmospheric pressure, a thousandth of a bar, measures some amount of pressure.

clue.text: A stink about record being returned

definitions.note: by the setter's special rule, an 'A' opening a clue always means astronomer

indicators.note: turned back, so the whole run is read right to left
the stink goes around the record

parts.note: reek means a strong bad smell
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A fuss about a record being sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts the record inside the stink, and 'being returned' then reads the whole run backwards. By the setter's rule, 'A' means astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Kepler set out the laws of planetary motion.

clue.text: Synthetic material not for fat boy, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: a boy who is not fat might be Terry, lean

explanation.surface: A synthetic fabric unsuitable for a plump lad.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry is a boy's name, and lean is the opposite of fat: TERRY LEAN, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Terylene is a British trade name for polyester fibre, a man-made fabric.
